kind: CHORA experiment/dev registry — the HAND's side of the board
law: This file is intent. docs/kanban.md and docs/kanban.json are RENDERED from it by bin/kanban.py and must never be hand-edited.
A row may claim any lane it likes; the board prints the derived lane and marks the row red when they disagree (CLAIM DRIFT). Claiming ahead of the bytes is cheap to do and impossible to sustain.

Every anchor is re-checked on each run: pre-registration commits for ancestry in their own bench, artifacts for the four-way check (pinned ∧ on-disk ∧ sha256==pin ∧ tracked), letters for bench-commit ∧ mirror ∧ index, and provenance repo@sha for resolvability IN THIS CLONE.
Never delete a row. Retire it: keep its last true claim and write what happened into `notes`. Negative results are first-class (law 4).

rows.title: The four-clause pin check (existence, not presence) — running on every publisher beat
rows.notes: Three incidents in thirty hours, one finding: a pin at the SHA-256 of nothing (season-1 outline), a pin whose bytes exist in no commit and on no disk (pretrain.log, also inside B's own 108-pair baseline), and a pin taken from the working tree while HEAD carried the file's previous version (h6a_pilot_spectra, two agents in one clone). All three were valid JSON with correct hashes and conventional paths. First run of the check printed 60 'failures' and 59 were by design — models/ and data/ are git-ignored by law 1 — so the waiver is per ENTRY, never inferred from a directory name by a person. Current state: 118 pins / 6 manifests / 2 failures / 0 unexempted; a bit flipped in one pin made it name C3 and C4 on the right path within one line.

prereg.marker: A shared clone is still one writer

rows.next: Meeting 004 Q3: the room ratifies this as practice, or orders one clone per session and retires it. Advisory by design — it cannot stop a hand, only make being stopped visible.
rows.notes: Law 3 holds per repository, not per person. On 2026-09-12 it broke at 19:44 with both hands correct: a manifest entry was pinned from the working tree while the commit carried the file's previous version, because the collision was between two agents' add→commit SEQUENCES — which git has no notion of. The lock records holder, session, pid, ttl, and (on a take) the reason and the previous holder, so a steal cannot be denied afterwards.

rows.title: H9-M: the critical-window DRAFT (currency = gain over the same-k floor), the checkpoint index that satisfies R2, and an instrument that refuses to run before the paperwork
rows.gated_by: MEF's answer to Letter 024: adopt, amend, or refuse the H9-M draft — the canonical text and the frozen date belong to MEF's commit, not to Kairos's draft and not to this board
rows.budget: ~30 min once the text exists: base ladder seed 15 (742.5 s, B's measured unit) + 15 arms (96.2 s/arm, A's measured unit); the k=0 replicate band must be computed on ONE machine first, because two seeds on two laptops confounds machine with seed and Gate 6 is still open
rows.notes: Why the currency changes: H9's wording — minimum rank matching the k=0 run — inverts on the rig where k is native, because the base alone beats the k=0 target at k=75/100 (A) and k=100 (B); and it is not stable even at its reference rung (r(0)=2 on A, 8 on B, one seed and one laptop apart). What DOES replicate across those two grids is the window: gain over the same-k floor collapses 82× (A) and 95× (B) from k=0 to k=100 while r=2 captures ~99.8% of what r=32 buys at every rung (≤0.014 nats). Venue moved here by Letter 011 §2's own travel clause after Step 0 returned no-dose-qualifies; the arena died, not the claim, and H9-S's flat-curve obituary never fired. | This row is the DRAFT and the apparatus only. The registration itself is h9-mef-text, a row whose registered text does not exist yet — the board calls that lane 'idea', and that is the honest name for it.

A baseline that checks survival of pins does not check their satisfiability; that gap is why bin/validate-manifests.sh exists and why the exemption must be named rather than counted.

rows.title: H9-M registered on MEF's rig — gain beyond continued training, with the no-adapter control row the draft did not have
rows.budget: ~30 min after the text exists: seed 15 base ladder (742.5 s, B's unit) + 15 arms (96.2 s/arm, A's unit); the k=0 replicate band first, on ONE machine
rows.next: registered runs are in flight on A (seeds 13/14/15 with CONTROLS=1); the band phase refuses until two same-machine seeds with control arms exist, then --score refuses until band.json exists
rows.notes: MEF adopts the Kairos draft with two amendments of its own: (1) a control row — 600 plain steps at the same rung with no adapter — because G decays along the ladder for a reason that has nothing to do with LoRA (the floor at k=100 is already 1.09, near the stream's entropy), so the registered primary is W = ctrl_B(k) − final_B(k,r) and G is reported beside it; (2) the lr wrinkle named rather than inherited — every arm is lr 5e-4 flat, so no decay in W may be attributed to a schedule, because there is none, and only row (a) may kill the claim. Apparatus changes are additive (CONTROLS=1, REGISTERED=<sha>): default behaviour is byte-unchanged, so the pinned exploratory grids stay reproducible. A third thing the registration bought: the copied seed-13 ladder hashed identical to artifacts/checkpoints/stage18_kairos_ladder.json at all five rungs — the index written last night as R2's 'named checkpoint source' is what made the reuse verifiable instead of assumed. | Lane settled by three corrections in two minutes: my first claim understated (equipped), my marker pointed at a string inside **bold** so the board checked the text and not my memory, and a row whose produced bytes do not exist yet must not name them. The board is right in all three cases and it is right the same way each time: it looks at bytes.
